app.title: RapidQuant — Lateral Flow Strip Quantification with Standard Curves and Limit of Detection
app.summary: The person picks a workflow (single strip, limit-of-detection series or unknown quantification) and fills in an experiment form: a name, a concentration unit, the replicate count and the concentration levels of the standards. Next they bring in strip photos from the live camera, the gallery or a folder. They confirm each photo, give each strip its standard concentration or mark it as an unknown with a sample ID and a dilution factor, and start quantification. Each strip is cropped automatically, and its test and control bands are measured as peak areas to give a T/C ratio. The standards are fitted with a 4PL or 5PL curve, chosen by statistical test, which gives the limit of blank and limit of detection, back-calculated recoveries and unknown concentrations with prediction intervals. Suspect high readings can be checked against a diluted strip for hook effect. The experiment is saved and can be exported as a ZIP or a combined PDF of figures, a summary table and raw data.

task.text: Turn photos of lateral flow test strips into band-intensity ratios, fit a calibration curve to the standards, and report the limit of detection and the concentrations of unknown samples.

data.text: Photos of assay test strips, each tagged with an assigned standard concentration or marked as an unknown sample. From each photo the code computes a 1D band intensity profile, band areas and a T/C ratio. These are pooled into a concentration–response table, and saved experiments are kept as records on the device.
data.item: a photographed lateral flow test strip with a control band and a test band

stage.text: quantifying assay strips into a calibration curve and unknown concentrations, right after running the strips

mechanism.text: A step-by-step flow (setup form, then strip loader, then results) gathers labelled strip images. The rest is disabled until the required fields are filled and at least one strip is loaded. A batch run then fills a results screen that holds the calibration-curve figure, a model audit card with fitted parameters and limits, an unknowns table with zone flags, and per-strip chromatogram cards that can be zoomed and downloaded.

field.text: lateral flow immunoassay densitometry and calibration in bioanalytical chemistry

workflow.name: fit a standard curve to measured standards and read unknowns off it

steps.step: define the experiment and its standard levels
steps.here: A form takes the experiment name, a concentration unit (or a custom one), the replicate count n=1–3 and a list of concentration levels, with preset series. Continue stays disabled until the name and the levels are filled in.
Strip photos come from the live camera (with torch and tap-to-focus), the native camera, the gallery or a whole folder. Each capture is shown for a retake-or-confirm check before it is added.

steps.step: label each item with its role and known value
steps.here: Each loaded strip gets a standard concentration, typed or picked from the preset levels, or is switched to an unknown with a sample ID and a dilution factor (1x–100x). Strips can be previewed or removed.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Start Quantification runs a progress overlay. For each strip, two on-device detectors crop it and find its bands, and the background-subtracted band areas give a T/C ratio. The standards are then fitted with 4PL or 5PL, chosen by F-test and AICc.

steps.step: check the fit and the limits
steps.here: An audit card shows the model formula, why that model was chosen, the parameters a–d, LoB, LoD, the linear dynamic range, the saturation threshold and a standards recovery table. Per-strip chromatogram cards show T/C, the band areas and the figure.

Unknowns are listed with T/C, a concentration ± prediction interval and a zone badge (linear, saturated, hook suspect). 'Verify 1:10 Dilution' takes a photo of a diluted strip and either confirms the true low value or applies a ×10 corrected concentration.

The experiment is saved on the device and listed among saved experiments. Export writes a ZIP archive or a combined PDF with a CSV summary, raw JSON, the standard curve and the strip chromatograms, either to the last-used location or to a new one.

distinctive: The signal is read from photos: each strip is auto-cropped, its control and test bands are located, and the background-subtracted band areas give a test/control ratio
The curve model is picked automatically between 4PL and 5PL by an extra-sum-of-squares F-test and AICc, and the reason is shown
Limit of blank and limit of detection follow a named clinical lab standard (CLSI EP17-A2), with back-calculated recovery of the standards against an acceptance band
Unknowns carry dilution factors and a zone flag, and a suspected hook (prozone) effect can be checked by photographing a 1:10 diluted strip
Three modes (single strip, LoD series, unknown quantification) share one setup → load → results flow
